name: Table 1-6: Body
_doc: Determines the body type (size category) of a Planet. Roll on the Rocky or Gas Giant subtable based on the Planet's nature.

rocky_planets.name: Low-Mass
rocky_planets.description: The world is even lower in mass than its small size would suggest. Apply -7 to the result of any roll on Table 1-7: Gravity. Generate Resources and Environments as if the world was Small. Mineral Resource deposits cannot exceed Limited in abundance.

rocky_planets.name: Small
rocky_planets.description: This world lacks the mass and size to support significant gravity or resources. Apply -5 to the result of any roll on Table 1-7: Gravity.

rocky_planets.name: Small and Dense
rocky_planets.description: Generate Resources and Environments as if the world was Small. Add +10 to the result of any roll on Table 1-19: Resource Abundance for any Mineral Resources.

rocky_planets.name: Large
rocky_planets.description: Worlds of this size can range across a vast spectrum of possible types.

rocky_planets.name: Large and Dense
rocky_planets.description: Add +5 to the result of any roll on Table 1-7: Gravity. Generate Resources and Environments as if the world was Large. Add +10 to the result of any roll on Table 1-19: Resource Abundance for any Mineral Resources.

rocky_planets.name: Vast
rocky_planets.description: Huge and voluminous, worlds of this type strain the upper edges of the possible size for a single world. Add +4 to the result of any roll on Table 1-7: Gravity.

gas_giants.name: Gas Dwarf
gas_giants.description: Smaller than a typical gas giant but more massive than most rocky Planets. Apply -5 to the result of any roll on Table 1-7: Gravity.

gas_giants.name: Gas Giant
gas_giants.description: Typical gas giants are vastly more massive than almost any other world, and tend to have correspondingly powerful gravitational effects.

gas_giants.name: Massive Gas Giant
gas_giants.description: The largest gas giants can rival weaker stars. Add +3 to the result of any roll on Table 1-7: Gravity. Any Massive Gas Giant not in the Inner Cauldron has a chance of being one of these titans: roll 1d10; on 8+, count the result on Table 1-7 as 10, and its moons are generated as if they were one Solar Zone closer to their star.
gas_giants.special_rule: If not in Inner Cauldron, roll 1d10; on 8+ treat gravity roll as 10 and generate moons as if one Solar Zone closer to the star.
